clue.text: Erratic method of painting round the bend

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk
round the bend is British slang for mad, which is mental

explanation.surface: A painter's technique so wild it seems to have gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone erratic is moody and unpredictable, a classic synonym.

clue.text: Deception involving a lady, you may find

definitions.text: Deception involving a lady, you may find

parts.words: Deception involving a lady, you may find
parts.note: a street swindle where the mark must 'find the lady', picking out the queen among three face-down playing cards

explanation.surface: A con trick in which a woman is involved, as you may discover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you may find' completes the phrase 'find the lady', the patter of the card sharp running the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The cryptic reading describes the find-the-lady card swindle itself.

clue.text: Sorcerer featured in American periodical first

indicators.note: first says the periodical piece comes ahead of the American piece

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: A wizard is the cover story in a US magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is one of the Magi, a wise man or magician.

clue.text: Sedate rite devised for this season

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A calm ceremony is invented to mark the time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges SEDATE RITE; 'this season' points to the clue's own subject, a church season.
explanation.definitionFit: The Easter season in the church calendar, the weeks following Easter Day.

clue.text: An offer to take off a pound, by the way

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: take off tells us letters are removed from the word before it

parts.note: a proposal is an offer
a gives A and L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (libra)

explanation.surface: Someone makes a bid to knock a pound off the price, incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take off' removes A and L from the end of PROPOSAL, leaving PROPOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is used to mean incidentally or in connection with.

clue.text: It may be dropped for the protection of the listener

definitions.text: It may be dropped for the protection of the listener

parts.words: It may be dropped for the protection of the listener
parts.note: a flap on a hat that is let down to cover and warm the hearing organ of the wearer

explanation.surface: Something lowered to shield an eavesdropper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listener' suggests a person listening; it is just the wearer's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes the hat flap pulled down over the ears in the cold.

clue.text: Set up new routine for performance in theatre

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means a word is written upwards, so its letters read in reverse

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A fresh routine is established for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns RUT into TUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a single act or routine on a variety stage.

clue.text: Profitable development of vital cure

indicators.note: development of suggests the words are reshaped into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Developing a life-saving remedy brings in a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges VITAL CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative business is money-making, that is profitable.

clue.text: Pupil possibly, is a personal favourite

definitions.meaning: the pupil of the eye is literally the apple of it, the old name for that part
a person who is cherished above all others

explanation.surface: A school pupil may be the teacher's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' suggests a schoolchild, but it is the opening in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase originally named the pupil and now means a dearly loved person.

clue.text: Doctor is great disaster in case of bishop

indicators.note: in case of means placed inside the outer casing of the next piece

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor says a bishop's case is a great catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' tempts an anagram signal, but it is the definition; 'disaster' is the anagram signal, and 'in case of' puts the jumble inside the bishop's RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is a grade of hospital doctor in Britain, below consultant.

clue.text: With due deference, runs over summing-up

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pace, from Latin, means with due respect to
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Politely, someone goes over a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole run. Pace, said as two syllables, is used before a name to mean 'with respect to (someone who may disagree)'.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap, short for recapitulation, is a summary.

clue.text: Woman in carriage is leaning backwards

indicators.note: backwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lady in a coach is tilting backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EISLE sits within 'carriage is leaning'; 'in' signals the hidden run and 'backwards' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a woman's given name.

clue.text: European sometimes employed in a vault

definitions.meaning: a native of Poland is a European
the long flexible rod used by athletes in the vault event

explanation.surface: A European occasionally used in a crypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' suggests a crypt or bank vault; it is the athletics jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a person from Poland, and the rod used in pole-vaulting.

clue.text: The sort of bar runners may jump

definitions.text: The sort of bar runners may jump

parts.words: The sort of bar runners may jump
parts.note: a bar crossing the cricket stumps, and also security money for release that absconders skip out on

explanation.surface: A hurdle that athletes might leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' suggests athletes, but it is people fleeing justice who 'jump' it; it is also a crosspiece on cricket stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Bail is both a crossbar on the wicket and money that a fleeing defendant forfeits.

clue.text: Book that French produced about English style of architecture

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the pieces surround the next letter

parts.note: Romans is a book of the New Testament
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A French-language book about English architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like it wants the French roman, but it is the Bible's ROMANS; 'produced' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanesque is the round-arched building style of Europe before Gothic.

clue.text: Good friend brings a tea set back

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: back means the word is written in reverse order

explanation.surface: A good friend brings round a tea service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SET into TES. Achates was the faithful companion of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates, loyal friend of Aeneas, became a byword for a faithful companion.

clue.text: Its cells are constructed by workers in the colonies

definitions.text: Its cells are constructed by workers in the colonies

parts.words: Its cells are constructed by workers in the colonies
parts.note: worker bees in hives build a wax structure of six-sided chambers

explanation.surface: Prison cells built by labourers in the overseas territories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cells' and 'colonies' suggest prisons and empire; they are a bee colony's wax chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexagonal wax structure made by bees to store honey.

clue.text: Condition is accepted by college head? No way!

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the next piece
No tells us the word for way is dropped

parts.note: a provost is the head of some colleges
ST, street, is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rule is agreed by the head of college, who then refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way!' reads as an exclamation of refusal but signals dropping the street from the college head; 'accepted by' then takes IS inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Racket found behind sandhill in faraway port

indicators.note: behind says the racket piece follows the sandhill piece

parts.note: a dune is a hill of sand
din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Noise is heard beyond the dunes at a distant harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a port city in the South Island of New Zealand, far from Britain.

clue.text: He reports cardinal embracing saint

indicators.note: embracing means wrapped around the next piece

parts.note: John Henry Newman was a famous English cardinal

explanation.surface: A journalist covers a cardinal hugging a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' tempts N, E, S or W as compass points; it is Cardinal Newman.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a reporter or journalist.

clue.text: Old boy returning after to identify psychological medicine

indicators.note: after says the returning piece comes after the identify piece

parts.note: to place someone is to identify them

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: A former pupil comes back to pin down a mind cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns OB into BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill whose effect is purely on the patient's mind.

clue.text: Tenor taking unmixed wine out East

indicators.note: out says a letter is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: pure means unmixed
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A singer drinks neat wine abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' suggests a singer, but it means general sense. 'out' removes E from PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The purport of something is its gist or meaning, as is its tenor.

clue.text: Reportedly put up beams

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to put up is to raise

explanation.surface: Joists were said to have been erected.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are beams of light.

clue.text: Vessel in East you and I take on river

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.surface: A ship in the east that the two of us take upriver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship; it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large water jug, a vessel for liquid.

clue.text: Escape in time just before receiving notice

indicators.note: receiving means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: eve is the time just before an event
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Getting away in time, just before getting a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or avoid.

clue.text: A question a sailor raised in Asian port

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means written upwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor brought up a query at an eastern harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AB into BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqaba is Jordan's port on the Red Sea, in western Asia.

clue.text: Guy supporting suspension of action

definitions.meaning: a guy is a supporting rope, as on a mast or tent

explanation.surface: A man backing a halt to proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' suggests a man; it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a bracing rope or wire, and a postponement of legal proceedings.

clue.text: Farm's produce cut by measure

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened at its end

parts.note: a crop is farm produce
FT, foot, is a measure

explanation.surface: A farm's harvest is reduced by some amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter P from CROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Doctor operating? Friend reduced Cynthia's tremor

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
on means operating, working

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a Quaker is a member of the Society of Friends

explanation.surface: A surgeon at work? A friend calmed Cynthia's shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts R off QUAKER. Cynthia is a name of Artemis, the moon goddess, so her tremor is a lunar one.
explanation.definitionFit: A seismic tremor on the Moon, which Cynthia, the moon goddess, personifies.

clue.text: Quite unacceptable, being too much for anaemic people

definitions.meaning: outside the bounds of decent behaviour

definitions.text: being too much for anaemic people
definitions.meaning: read literally, further than the pallid can go, as if pale people had a limit

explanation.surface: Something outrageous, too much for sickly folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'pale' as pallid people rather than a boundary fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means outside the limits of acceptable conduct.
